note: Generated Codex types: linguist-generated, GENERATED header, one regeneration command, one copy only, and a unit test that compares a recorded digest on every run (CI) and regenerates byte for byte when the CLI is installed.

Every app and package README states its purpose, public surface and dependency direction; the @aether/* dependency lists equal package.json and the forbidden imports are the ones scripts/check-boundaries.mjs enforces.
Twelve ADRs, each with status and date, all listed in the index.
Cross-package rules and limits live in packages/contracts (for example CLOCK_OUT_MAX_SESSIONS) and role matrices in packages/kernel; sampled by one reviewer only, the charter asks for two.
Negative tests cover authorization, CSRF, Host and Origin (DNS rebinding), path traversal, SSRF and the public-route sweep; refactors were preceded by pinning tests (see the test(...): pin commits).

Phone, tablet and desktop screenshots of every route were reviewed by the maintainer-side agent only (no independent reviewer); the viewed cells and the defects found and fixed are listed in docs/verification/ux-matrix.md.
D01 to D20 are closed in the code with a guarding test each, except D16: the real VoiceOver and TalkBack pass is a human step in the publishing checklist.
No real-device field report exists yet; the steps to capture one are in docs/getting-started.md and docs/release/publishing-checklist.md.
Deterministic A/B figures (bytes, draw calls, triangles, heap) are recorded; the timing A/B of at least eight interleaved rounds could not run on a loaded machine.
All community files exist; pnpm run oss:check passes.
Both READMEs have the same ten sections: what it is, quick start, limits, privacy, providers, documentation, contributing, licence; the AI-assistance and unofficial statements are present.
Tutorial, how-to, reference and explanation pages are indexed in docs/README.md; no documentation file is unreferenced.
Maintainer notes are split into docs/internal with a dated index; personal paths, host names and addresses were removed from them and oss:check is clean.
Every ADR and design record carries a status and a date; internal notes are dated snapshots in their index.

The release history is built with trailers dropped (every maintainer trailer; from the upstream commits only the session links and AI co-author lines, human co-authors stay) and private strings rewritten; history-verify checks that no commit keeps a session link or AI co-author trailer. The AI-assistance statement is in the README and provenance.
Strategy C: upstream commits kept as they were, the maintainer work as milestones whose bodies list what they contain and why.
The figures on the page are the ones measured by the plan, apply and verify runs named on it.
A CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM is generated from the lockfile (every shipped package has a licence and a purl); the release checklist covers version, tag, SBOM and provenance.

More than twenty concrete limits and defaults in the document were compared with the constants in the code (stream clients, pending requests, wait times, file modes, rate limits) and match; the public-route sweep and the negative tests are in the suite.

The only outbound connections in the code are the opt-in connectors, the runner and hook calls to the control plane, and the opt-in A2A gateway; no telemetry or CDN exists, and docs/how-to.md lists how to back up and remove everything AETHER wrote.

The human steps (name and trademark, private reporting, repository settings, real-device and screen-reader checks, final go or no-go) are written as a checklist; the real-device, screen-reader and trademark-search steps have not been carried out.
